Roles, the installer line: a developer who sets up invoicer's command on each accountant's machine, so the accountant installs nothing. Installing Python is left to the README setup section, by the names decision.
Roles: the accountant and installer items, each named by its job.

Throughout: `invoicer` stands alone only in the title and as the owner in `invoicer`'s command; `invoicer`'s command is what prints in the one way and in each idea; `accountant` for one who prints; the accountant's machine in Roles and O2; no runtime named anywhere.
Objectives and key results, the O1 item, ending in without anyone's help.
Objectives and key results, the O2 item.
Objectives and key results: KR1.2 runs from opening the spreadsheet to the printed invoice; KR2.1 and KR2.2 run from starting a setup to invoicer's command running for the accountant.

Objectives and key results: KR1.1 counts only invoices where invoicer's command runs that needed someone's help or had a wrong total; KR1.2, KR2.1 and KR2.2 as decided, each Lower is better; the ranking stated once, in the template's ranking line as `KR1.1` and `KR2.1` comes first, with no rank notes on the key result lines; the template's no-targets and Goodhart lines carry the rest.

Objectives and key results: the command and the README part for the accountant are measured by O1's key results, and the README setup section by O2's; the vision names each objective once, so a maintainer places each piece by the role it serves.
Concept, the one way: `invoicer`'s command prints the finished invoice from the invoice lines in the `accountant`'s spreadsheet, plus the client's tax rate.
Concept, the three ideas: The spreadsheet as it is; Nothing wrong prints, naming the line or value to fix; The rate given each time, with no rate remembered.

Concept: the installer's moment holds by the first and third ideas (the sheet taken as it is, the rate given each time, so nothing to configure); the accountant's moments of giving the lines and the rate, and of the invoice or the message, hold by all three ideas.
Concept: each of the three idea lines ends in for `O1`, and none names O2.
